query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: High-throughput computational thermodynamic modeling combined with experimental validation can accurately and efficiently determine the melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy (HEA) family.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys with varying compositions, typically consisting of five or more principal elements in near-equiatomic proportions.
generation.intervention: Application of high-throughput computational thermodynamic modeling (e.g., CALPHAD or machine learning-based approaches) followed by targeted experimental validation using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and dilatometry.
generation.conditions: The HEAs are modeled and tested under controlled atmospheric conditions to prevent oxidation or contamination, with temperatures ranging from room temperature to above their melting points.
generation.structural_mediator: The multicomponent phase equilibria and atomic interactions in the HEA system, as captured by the computational model and validated by experimental data.
generation.mechanism: The computational model predicts thermodynamic properties by leveraging databases of phase diagrams and thermodynamic parameters, while experimental techniques provide direct measurements to refine and validate the predictions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The combined approach will yield melting temperatures, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties with an accuracy of ±5% compared to experimental benchmarks, across a wide range of HEA compositions.
generation.baseline: Current methods relying solely on experimental measurements or computational predictions, which are either time-consuming or less accurate for complex HEA systems.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to work well for HEAs with well-characterized constituent elements and thermodynamic databases but may be less accurate for systems with poorly understood interactions or metastable phases.
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of predictions may vary for HEAs with significant short-range ordering or non-equilibrium phases, which are challenging to model computationally.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a diverse set of HEA compositions, perform high-throughput computational modeling to predict their thermodynamic properties, and validate these predictions with experimental measurements using DSC and dilatometry.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted thermodynamic properties consistently deviate by more than ±5% from experimental measurements across the tested HEA compositions, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
